links.targetTitle: srUSDS makes losses visible as a falling conversion rate rat

title: External senior capital can only convert at the monthly settlement, because capital that is instantly redeemable cannot absorb losses
content:
A.3.2.2.4.2.2 gives srUSDS two queues: users "can add USDS to the deposit queue for conversion into srUSDS; or add srUSDS to the redemption queue for conversion back into USDS at any point during the month," and "assets placed in either queue can be withdrawn by the user at any time before the Monthly Settlement Cycle begins." At settlement, everything remaining is processed at the prevailing conversion rate.

The batching is not an implementation convenience — it is what makes the instrument coherent. A.3.2.1.2.1 requires Total Risk Capital to be "currently deployable towards covering its Required Risk Capital obligations," and A.3.2.2.4.3.6 gives originated senior capital a one-month life. Capital that a depositor could pull mid-month would fail both tests: a Prime Agent cannot rely on it to cover a requirement, and the monthly auction cannot allocate a pool whose size is unknown.

So the queue converts an open-ended retail deposit into a month-long commitment, synchronized with the same cycle that sets the conversion rate, runs the origination auction, allocates losses and collects penalties. The Monthly Settlement Cycle is effectively the system's clock, and every claim in the risk-capital stack is defined relative to it.

The free-withdrawal-before-settlement rule is the concession that keeps the instrument attractive: a depositor is committed only from the settlement boundary, not from the moment of deciding. The cost is borne at the other end — a holder who wants out must wait for the next settlement and accept whatever the conversion rate has become by then, including a loss booked after they queued.
description: srUSDS deposit and redemption queues accept entries any time and permit free withdrawal beforehand, but all queued amounts process together at the Monthly Settlement Cycle at the prevailing rate.
